# Matching evaluation (synthetic)

Offline harness for the matching pipeline. It runs the production code paths (retrieval,
understanding, scoring, lead selection) in a throwaway database.

**Every dataset is synthetic.** The records were generated by `generate_dataset.py` from a fixed seed.
They are invented, not real user reports. Coordinates are public campus place points from
`app/geo/uet_lahore.json`. Photos are rendered from simple coloured silhouettes, not real photographs.
The numbers describe these datasets only. They are not measured accuracy on real lost-and-found reports.

## Datasets

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `data/synthetic_pairs.json` (`--dataset base`) | 50 lost queries across 10 item types, 50 true pairs, 250 hard negatives, 30 unrelated found reports. No photos. |
| `data/synthetic_pairs_extended.json` (`--dataset extended`) | The base set, plus synthetic photos on every report, plus 350 targeted hard negatives (50 per type, 7 types). 680 found reports in total. |

Hard-negative types (each built to look like its query's item, and each a different physical item):

- `hn-lookalike`: same type, colour and brand, found days later at another spot
- `hn-brand`: different brand (`hn-nearby` for item types without a brand list)
- `hn-colour`: different colour
- `hn-before-loss`: found before the loss
- `hn-category`: same colour at the same place, different item type
- `hx-nearby-same`: same colour and category, nearby spot, no brand or feature
- `hx-brand`: different brand, where the item type has a brand list
- `hx-feature`: different distinctive feature
- `hx-same-place-other`: same place, different item type
- `hx-visual`: visually similar (same silhouette and colour), different item type
- `hx-missing-brand`: found report with no brand
- `hx-missing-feature`: found report with no distinctive feature

Limits of the data that matter for reading the results:

- Brand mismatch is only visible to the scorer when both sides state a brand. About half of the lost
  queries do not state one, so many `hn-brand` and `hx-brand` negatives cannot be told apart from a match.
- The templated descriptions carry identity words almost only through the structured fields (category,
  colour, brand, feature). Real descriptions will probably give the description signal more to work with.
- True pairs often share only colour and place. Under an identity rule they cannot notify.

## Metrics

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| precision@1 | Of queries with a true match, the share whose top-ranked candidate is that match. Ranking only, no threshold. |
| recall at threshold | True pairs that would notify (Strong or Possible lead, capped per query). |
| recall (retrieved) | True pairs that survive candidate retrieval at any score. |
| FPR (all) | Notified non-matching pairs ÷ all non-matching pairs. |
| FPR (hard) | Notified hard negatives built for the same query ÷ all hard negatives. |
| notification precision | True notified ÷ all notified. |
| notifications per query | Notified pairs per query. Measures notification load. |
| weak leads per query | Weak leads stored but not notified. Visibility load for owners. |
| FPR by hard type | Notified ÷ population, per hard-negative type. |

## Run

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m evaluation.run_eval --label my-run --dataset base
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m evaluation.run_eval --label my-run --dataset extended
```

Environment switches (for comparisons): `MATCH_SCORER=v1|v2` (default v2), `MATCH_TEXT_METHOD=bm25|hashing`
(default bm25). Results are written to `results/<label>.json`, including the false-positive examples with
their explanations.

## Results

All numbers come from the files in `results/`. The original scorer is the code at commit `6837163`,
before any of the matching work below. Each row uses the same dataset.

### Original set (`base`)

| Scorer | P@1 | Recall at threshold | FPR all | FPR hard | Notif. precision | Notif./query | Weak/query |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original scorer (`orig-base`) | 80.0% | 100.0% | 2.0% | 58.4% | 13.0% | 7.68 | 0 |
| v1 weighted, identity-free description (`phase3a-description-base`) | 66.0% | 90.0% | 0.6% | 24.8% | 30.0% | 3.00 | 0 |
| **v2 (default)** (`phase3-v2-base`) | 56.0% | 22.0% | 0.1% | **2.0%** | **47.8%** | **0.46** | 8.3 |

### Extended set (`extended`, with targeted hard negatives and synthetic photos)

| Scorer | P@1 | Recall at threshold | FPR all | FPR hard | Notif. precision | Notif./query | Weak/query |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original scorer (`orig-extended`) | 18.0% | 96.0% | 1.3% | 54.3% | 9.7% | 9.90 | 0 |
| Phase 2, BM25 description (`phase2-bm25-extended`) | 18.0% | 58.0% | 0.4% | 19.7% | 19.3% | 3.00 | 0 |
| v1 fallback (`phase3-v1-fallback-extended`) | 6.0% | 30.0% | 0.4% | 21.8% | 10.0% | 3.00 | 0 |
| **v2 (default)** (`phase3-v2-extended`) | 12.0% | 22.0% | 0.1% | **1.8%** | **36.7%** | **0.60** | 21.6 |

FPR (hard) by type, extended set:

| Type | Original scorer | v1 fallback | v2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| hx-nearby-same | 98% | 52% | 0% |
| hx-missing-feature | 100% | 74% | 10% |
| hx-missing-brand | 98% | 54% | 0% |
| hx-feature | 94% | 42% | 6% |
| hx-brand | 64% | 26% | 0% |
| hn-lookalike | 78% | 0% | 0% |
| hn-brand | 58% | 10% | 0% |
| hn-colour | 54% | 4% | 6% |
| hx-visual | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| hx-same-place-other | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| hn-category | 4% | 0% | 0% |
| hn-before-loss | 0% | 0% | 0% |

`hx-visual` and `hx-same-place-other` are zero for every scorer because the category gate rejects them.
The rule "a visually similar photo alone never notifies" is covered by a unit test, not by this set.

### Reading the results honestly

- v2 cuts the false-positive rates sharply. It also cuts recall at threshold, from 90% to 22% on the
  original set and from 30% (v1) to 22% on the extended set. Most of that loss is true pairs that share only
  colour and place. Under the rule, they stay Weak leads and do not notify.
- Precision@1 is poor on both sets for every scorer. On the extended set the top-ranked candidate is often a
  hard negative that shares brand, colour and place with the query. The scorer cannot tell these apart from
  the lost report alone.
- The v2 qualification rule was revised once, after the first measurement. Brand plus colour alone was
  notifying (many black JanSport bags are on campus), so brand now needs a description match, while a
  matching feature qualifies on its own. The earlier numbers are kept in `v2a-base.json` and `v2a-extended.json`,
  and `v2b-extended.json` records the revised rule before the typed-feature colour fix. The final numbers are
  in `phase3-v2-*.json`.
- Phase 3a (description signal) on its own: removing place names, boilerplate and digits from the
  description, treating a missing description as absent, and removing the retrieval top-50 cut. The top-50
  cut was dropping true matches. See `phase3a-description*.json`.

### Earlier history

| File | Note |
|---|---|
| `baseline.json` | First baseline (precision@1 80%, hard FPR 58.4%). Measured on the base set with the original scorer. This file was overwritten by a re-measurement after the dataset fix, so it now holds the corrected numbers. |
| `phase1-extraction.json` | After extraction changes (colour shades, aliases, models, typed features). Base set. |
| `phase2-bm25.json` | After BM25 description similarity. Base set. |
| `after-steps-1-7.json` | After the lifecycle and evidence steps. Base set, same numbers as the original scorer. |

## Limits

- Templated text is easier than real descriptions. Recall here is likely optimistic for description signals
  and pessimistic for identity rules, because the templates rarely state identifying details.
- No Roman-Urdu or misspelled descriptions are included.
- Only lost-side queries are evaluated. Found-side queries are not measured.
- Hard negatives are constructed by rules. They do not cover the full range of real look-alikes.
- Photos are synthetic silhouettes, so the visual signal behaves very differently from real photographs.
